## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical containment across identity, data-at-rest controls, network segmentation, runtime monitoring, and automated rollback.

## Key Concepts

- Per-tenant IAM Conditions and Workload Identity
- CMEK and envelope encryption per tenant
- PSC and VPC Service Controls for network isolation
- Cloud IDS/Armor for real-time detection
- Automated containment playbooks with synthetic tenants for validation

gcloud run revisions delete <revision-name>

```bash
# Illustrative: create a per-tenant CMEK key
gcloud kms keys create tenantA-key --location us-central1 --keyring tenant-ring --purpose encryption

# Illustrative: configure per-tenant Workload Identity
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding tenantA-sa@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser \
  --member "serviceAccount:$PROJECT.svc.id.goog[tenantA-namespace/tenantA-sa]"

# Illustrative: apply per-tenant Pod Security Standard
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenantA-namespace
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
EOF
```

This question tests practical understanding of multi-tenant API isolation on GCP, focusing on real-world controls (API Gateway, IAM Conditions, quotas, logging) and automated verification.

## Key Concepts

- **CI automation**: Synthetic tenants, scoped-access tests, and automated rollback mechanisms ensure isolation policies remain effective

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical knowledge of tenant isolation using CMEK, IAM Conditions, and CI validation in a real GCP setup.

## Key Concepts
- Customer-managed keys (CMEK) per tenant
- IAM Conditions for fine-grained access control
- Rotation and auditing of KMS keys
- Bucket/object policies aligned to tenant prefixes
- CI automation for synthetic tenants and rollback

## Code Example
```json
{
  "bindings": [
    {
      "role": "roles/storage.objectAdmin",
      "members": ["serviceAccount:tenant-123-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"],
      "condition": {
        "title": "TenantIs123",
        "description": "Tenant-limited access to prefix",
        "expression": "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/buckets/my-bucket/objects/tenant-123/')"
      }
    }
  ],
  "version": 3
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test key rotation without impacting tenants?
- What alerts or dashboards would you set up for cross-tenant access attempts?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect data isolation in a multi-tenant GCP analytics stack using real controls (datasets, authorized views, IAM Conditions, CMEK, PSC/VPC-SC) and CI/CD gates that simulate tenants.

## Key Concepts
- Dataset-per-brand isolation within a shared project
- Authorized Views for per-brand data exposure
- IAM Conditions to enforce cross-brand access boundaries
- CMEK per brand for data-at-rest security
- Private Service Connect and VPC Service Controls for network containment
- CI/CD with synthetic tenants and rollback validation

## Code Example
```javascript
{
  "bindings": [
    {
      "role": "roles/bigquery.user",
      "members": ["serviceAccount:dataflow-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"],
      "condition": {
        "title": "BrandAOnly",
        "description": "Restrict access to BrandA dataset",
        "expression": "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/datasets/brandA')"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this to support new brands with zero downtime?
- How would you monitor and audit policy drift across datasets and keys, and automate rollback?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Junior engineers often implement long-lived, broad admin access. This question probes design for minimizing blast radius with JIT elevation, IAM Conditions, and robust auditing.

## Key Concepts
- Just-In-Time elevation with tenant scoping
- Access Context Manager + IAM Conditions
- Per-tenant service accounts and MFA
- Automatic revocation and rollback
- Auditing, canary tests, and rollback plans

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example IAM binding snippet (illustrative)
bindings:
  - role: roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin
    members:
      - "user:admin@example.com"
    condition:
      title: "TenantA-only-elevation"
      expression: "resource.name.startsWith('projects/PROJECT_ID/tenants/TENANT_A/')"
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the JIT policy and validate tenant isolation in CI/CD?
- How would you handle revocation if abuse is suspected without impacting tenants?
